top_reforms.description: Extension of flexicurity — easy hiring/firing combined with generous unemployment benefits and active labour market policies (ALMPs).
top_reforms.outcome: Unemployment stayed below 6% even through the Global Financial Crisis; one of the highest employment rates in the OECD.

top_reforms.reform: Pension reform — transition from defined-benefit to DC + mandatory labour market pensions (1987–2010)
top_reforms.description: Gradual shift to funded ATP / occupational pensions; increased private savings rate substantially.
top_reforms.outcome: Pension assets ~200% of GDP; sustainable public finances; reduced pressure on PAYG state pension.

top_reforms.reform: 2011 tax reform — shift from income to consumption taxes
top_reforms.description: Reduced marginal income tax rates; offset by higher environmental and property taxes; revenue-neutral.
top_reforms.outcome: Improved labour supply incentives; Denmark remained highest-taxing OECD country with strong growth.
